title: August 2026 - Liberty Street Economics
gist: This is the Liberty Street Economics August 2026 archive listing, so only the opening teasers of two posts were captured — the full post bodies and their results are absent. It shows the New York Fed publishing on two fronts that month: a new "Street Level" series by research director Kartik B. Athreya opening on how AI is reshaping the labor market and hiring, and a Guillaume Roussellet post using the sovereign bond term structure to gauge how precisely investors perceive r-star.

themes.theme: Street Level: NY Fed research director on AI and hiring

insights.claim: The New York Fed's research director Kartik B. Athreya launched "Street Level" on Liberty Street Economics in August 2026, a new recurring series that periodically synthesizes recent New York Fed Research staff analysis thematically and adds his own observations.
insights.speaker: Kartik B. Athreya
insights.so_what: A standing synthesis channel from the Fed's research director is a cheap read on which research themes the New York Fed considers policy-relevant — worth adding to the monitoring list.
insights.quote: My goal for this series is to periodically offer some thematic discussion of that work, highlighting recent analysis by Research staff and adding my own observations on the issue at hand.
insights.locator: AI’s Impact on Labor and Hiring (August 5, 2026)

insights.claim: The New York Fed's research director chose how artificial intelligence is changing the labor market and hiring behaviors as the inaugural topic of his new series, calling it "perhaps the hottest topic going" — a signal that AI's labor-market effects sit near the top of the Fed's research agenda in mid-2026.
insights.speaker: Kartik B. Athreya
insights.so_what: If the Fed's own research leadership treats AI-driven hiring shifts as the hottest question, expect AI-labor evidence to start feeding into how officials read employment data.
insights.quote: In this inaugural post, I’ll focus on perhaps the hottest topic going: How artificial intelligence is changing the labor market and hiring behaviors.
insights.locator: AI’s Impact on Labor and Hiring (August 5, 2026)

themes.theme: Reading r-star out of the bond term structure

insights.claim: In an August 2026 Liberty Street Economics post based on a recent Staff Report, Guillaume Roussellet uses the term structure of interest rates to study r-star — the natural real rate of return — and specifically how investors perceive it, rather than treating r-star as a single estimated level.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: A market-implied read on r-star perception gives a tradeable cross-check on term-premium and duration positioning; watch for the underlying Staff Report for the actual estimates.
insights.quote: In this post based on a recent Staff Report, we explore what the term structure of interest rates can teach us about r-star and its perception by investors.
insights.locator: A Window into Bond Investors’ Uncertainty About R‑Star (August 4, 2026)

insights.claim: How much information bond investors actually possess about r-star, and how precisely they know it, remains an open question that numerous papers have challenged — even though r-star acts as a guide for monetary policy decisions and policymakers read the sovereign bond term structure for market beliefs about future policy stance, inflation, and activity.
insights.speaker: Guillaume Roussellet
insights.so_what: If investor uncertainty about r-star is large, market-implied policy paths are noisier anchors than they look — a reason to fade confident long-end r-star narratives.
insights.quote: Numerous papers have questioned how much information investors possess, and how precisely they know r-star.
insights.locator: A Window into Bond Investors’ Uncertainty About R‑Star (August 4, 2026)
